checks.title: Table prefix
checks.summary: prefix shop_, 1 other install in the same schema
recommendations: Other WordPress installs share this database (old_). If they are leftovers, export them and drop their tables; shared schemas make backups and restores riskier.

checks.title: Database server
recommendations: MySQL 5.7 reached end of life on 2023-10-31 and no longer gets security fixes. Plan an upgrade to a supported LTS release.
innodb_buffer_pool_size is 1.0 GB but InnoDB data and indexes take 1.6 GB. On a dedicated database server give the buffer pool 50-70% of RAM.

checks.title: Autoloaded options

rows: WordPress core cron events (large means stuck or duplicate events)

recommendations: Every page load reads all autoloaded options; with a persistent object cache the whole set is one cache item, so keep it well under 1 MB.

Look at the largest options first. Leftovers from removed plugins can be deleted; settings of active plugins can often be switched to autoload 'off' (review the commented UPDATE statements in the fix plan).
Some transients are autoloaded. That happens when a plugin calls set_transient() without an expiry; report it to the plugin author.
The cron option is very large: list events with `wp cron event list` and remove duplicates left by deactivated plugins.

fixes.description: Stop autoloading wpseo_premium_redirects_export (1.6 MB); confirm the owning plugin reads it with get_option() only where needed
fixes.sql: UPDATE `shop_options` SET autoload = 'off' WHERE option_name = 'wpseo_premium_redirects_export'

fixes.description: Stop autoloading old_plugin_cache (200.0 KB); confirm the owning plugin reads it with get_option() only where needed
fixes.sql: UPDATE `shop_options` SET autoload = 'off' WHERE option_name = 'old_plugin_cache'

checks.title: Expired transients
checks.summary: 1,825 expired transients out of 9,120 stored (30.0 MB including timeouts)
recommendations: WP-CLI alternative that runs WordPress hooks: `wp transient delete --expired`.
Many expired transients usually mean WP-Cron is not running. If DISABLE_WP_CRON is set, make sure a system cron calls wp-cron.php.
A persistent object cache (Redis or Memcached) keeps transients out of the database entirely.

fixes.description: Delete 1,800 expired transients (value and timeout rows), as delete_expired_transients() does
fixes.sql: DELETE a, b FROM `shop_options` a INNER JOIN `shop_options` b ON b.option_name = CONCAT('_transient_', SUBSTRING(a.option_name, 20)) WHERE a.option_name LIKE '\_transient\_timeout\_%' AND CAST(a.option_value AS UNSIGNED) < UNIX_TIMESTAMP()

fixes.description: Delete 25 expired site transients
fixes.sql: DELETE a, b FROM `shop_options` a INNER JOIN `shop_options` b ON b.option_name = CONCAT('_site_transient_', SUBSTRING(a.option_name, 25)) WHERE a.option_name LIKE '\_site\_transient\_timeout\_%' AND CAST(a.option_value AS UNSIGNED) < UNIX_TIMESTAMP()

checks.title: Post revisions
checks.summary: 25,000 revisions for 800 posts (300.0 MB of content); 21,000 older than 30 days
recommendations: Revisions are unlimited. Add define( 'WP_POST_REVISIONS', 5 ); to wp-config.php to keep only the latest five per post.
WP-CLI alternative (runs WordPress hooks): `wp post delete $(wp post list --post_type=revision --format=ids) --force`.

fixes.description: Delete post meta of 21,000 revisions older than 30 days
fixes.sql: DELETE pm FROM `shop_postmeta` pm INNER JOIN `shop_posts` p ON p.ID = pm.post_id WHERE p.post_type = 'revision' AND p.post_modified_gmt < UTC_TIMESTAMP() - INTERVAL 30 DAY

fixes.description: Delete term relationships of 21,000 revisions older than 30 days
fixes.sql: DELETE tr FROM `shop_term_relationships` tr INNER JOIN `shop_posts` p ON p.ID = tr.object_id WHERE p.post_type = 'revision' AND p.post_modified_gmt < UTC_TIMESTAMP() - INTERVAL 30 DAY

fixes.description: Delete 21,000 revisions older than 30 days
fixes.sql: DELETE p FROM `shop_posts` p WHERE p.post_type = 'revision' AND p.post_modified_gmt < UTC_TIMESTAMP() - INTERVAL 30 DAY

checks.title: Auto-drafts
recommendations: 400 auto-drafts are older than 7 days, so the daily wp_scheduled_auto_draft_delete event is not running. Check WP-Cron (`wp cron event list`, DISABLE_WP_CRON and the system crontab).

fixes.description: Delete post meta of 400 auto-drafts older than 7 days
fixes.sql: DELETE pm FROM `shop_postmeta` pm INNER JOIN `shop_posts` p ON p.ID = pm.post_id WHERE p.post_status = 'auto-draft' AND p.post_date < NOW() - INTERVAL 7 DAY

fixes.description: Delete term relationships of 400 auto-drafts older than 7 days
fixes.sql: DELETE tr FROM `shop_term_relationships` tr INNER JOIN `shop_posts` p ON p.ID = tr.object_id WHERE p.post_status = 'auto-draft' AND p.post_date < NOW() - INTERVAL 7 DAY

fixes.description: Delete 400 auto-drafts older than 7 days
fixes.sql: DELETE p FROM `shop_posts` p WHERE p.post_status = 'auto-draft' AND p.post_date < NOW() - INTERVAL 7 DAY

checks.title: Trashed posts
checks.summary: 240 trashed posts, 200 trashed more than 30 days ago
recommendations: Emptying the trash in wp-admin (or `wp post delete ... --force`) runs plugin hooks; prefer it for WooCommerce products and orders.
WordPress empties the trash after EMPTY_TRASH_DAYS (30 by default) by cron; old trashed posts mean that event is not running.
Trashed WooCommerce orders found. With HPOS enabled, delete them in WooCommerce > Orders so the orders tables stay in sync.

fixes.description: Delete post meta of 200 trashed posts older than 30 days
fixes.sql: DELETE pm FROM `shop_postmeta` pm INNER JOIN `shop_posts` p ON p.ID = pm.post_id WHERE p.post_status = 'trash' AND p.post_modified_gmt < UTC_TIMESTAMP() - INTERVAL 30 DAY

fixes.description: Delete term relationships of 200 trashed posts older than 30 days
fixes.sql: DELETE tr FROM `shop_term_relationships` tr INNER JOIN `shop_posts` p ON p.ID = tr.object_id WHERE p.post_status = 'trash' AND p.post_modified_gmt < UTC_TIMESTAMP() - INTERVAL 30 DAY

fixes.description: Delete comment meta of comments on 200 trashed posts older than 30 days
fixes.sql: DELETE cm FROM `shop_commentmeta` cm INNER JOIN `shop_comments` c ON c.comment_ID = cm.comment_id INNER JOIN `shop_posts` p ON p.ID = c.comment_post_ID WHERE p.post_status = 'trash' AND p.post_modified_gmt < UTC_TIMESTAMP() - INTERVAL 30 DAY

fixes.description: Delete comments on 200 trashed posts older than 30 days
fixes.sql: DELETE c FROM `shop_comments` c INNER JOIN `shop_posts` p ON p.ID = c.comment_post_ID WHERE p.post_status = 'trash' AND p.post_modified_gmt < UTC_TIMESTAMP() - INTERVAL 30 DAY

fixes.description: Delete 200 trashed posts older than 30 days
fixes.sql: DELETE p FROM `shop_posts` p WHERE p.post_status = 'trash' AND p.post_modified_gmt < UTC_TIMESTAMP() - INTERVAL 30 DAY

checks.title: Spam and trashed comments
recommendations: After deleting comments directly, refresh the cached counts with `wp comment recount`.
Large spam volume: use an anti-spam plugin that discards obvious spam instead of storing it, or close comments on old posts.

fixes.description: Delete comment meta of spam and trashed comments
fixes.sql: DELETE cm FROM `shop_commentmeta` cm INNER JOIN `shop_comments` c ON c.comment_ID = cm.comment_id WHERE c.comment_approved IN ('spam', 'trash')

fixes.description: Delete 60,040 spam or trashed comments
fixes.sql: DELETE c FROM `shop_comments` c WHERE c.comment_approved IN ('spam', 'trash')

checks.title: Orphaned post meta
recommendations: Orphaned postmeta rows are left behind when posts are deleted with direct SQL or by plugins that skip the WordPress API. They are never read, so deleting them is safe.

fixes.description: Delete 54,000 orphaned postmeta rows whose post no longer exists
fixes.sql: DELETE m FROM `shop_postmeta` m LEFT JOIN `shop_posts` p ON p.ID = m.post_id WHERE p.ID IS NULL

checks.title: Orphaned term meta
recommendations: Orphaned termmeta rows are left behind when terms are deleted with direct SQL or by plugins that skip the WordPress API. They are never read, so deleting them is safe.

fixes.description: Delete 3 orphaned termmeta rows whose term no longer exists
fixes.sql: DELETE m FROM `shop_termmeta` m LEFT JOIN `shop_terms` p ON p.term_id = m.term_id WHERE p.term_id IS NULL

checks.title: Orphaned term relationships
checks.summary: 1,200 relationships to missing posts, 4 to missing terms
recommendations: Term counts may be off after cleanup; refresh them with `wp term recount category post_tag` (add product_cat, product_tag for WooCommerce).

fixes.description: Delete 1,200 term relationships of deleted posts
fixes.sql: DELETE r FROM `shop_term_relationships` r INNER JOIN `shop_term_taxonomy` tt ON tt.term_taxonomy_id = r.term_taxonomy_id LEFT JOIN `shop_posts` p ON p.ID = r.object_id WHERE p.ID IS NULL AND tt.taxonomy <> 'link_category'

fixes.description: Delete 4 term relationships of deleted terms
fixes.sql: DELETE r FROM `shop_term_relationships` r LEFT JOIN `shop_term_taxonomy` tt ON tt.term_taxonomy_id = r.term_taxonomy_id WHERE tt.term_taxonomy_id IS NULL

checks.title: Action Scheduler
checks.summary: 603,500 actions, 582,500 finished more than 30 days ago, 450 overdue
recommendations: Action Scheduler keeps finished actions for 30 days by default and cleans them in batches of 20 per run, which cannot keep up with busy stores. Lower the period with the action_scheduler_retention_period filter, or raise the batch size with action_scheduler_cleanup_batch_size.
450 pending actions are more than a day overdue: the queue runner is not keeping up. Check WP-Cron, or run the queue from system cron with `wp action-scheduler run`.
Most failed hooks: woocommerce_run_product_attribute_lookup_update (2,900). Their logs say why.

fixes.description: Delete log entries of finished actions older than 30 days
fixes.sql: DELETE l FROM `shop_actionscheduler_logs` l INNER JOIN `shop_actionscheduler_actions` a ON a.action_id = l.action_id WHERE a.status IN ('complete', 'failed', 'canceled') AND a.scheduled_date_gmt < UTC_TIMESTAMP() - INTERVAL 30 DAY

fixes.description: Delete 582,500 finished actions older than 30 days (complete, failed, canceled)
fixes.sql: DELETE FROM `shop_actionscheduler_actions` WHERE status IN ('complete', 'failed', 'canceled') AND scheduled_date_gmt < UTC_TIMESTAMP() - INTERVAL 30 DAY

fixes.description: Delete log entries whose action no longer exists
fixes.sql: DELETE l FROM `shop_actionscheduler_logs` l LEFT JOIN `shop_actionscheduler_actions` a ON a.action_id = l.action_id WHERE a.action_id IS NULL

checks.title: WooCommerce sessions
recommendations: WooCommerce removes expired sessions with the twice-daily woocommerce_cleanup_sessions event; a backlog means WP-Cron is not running. WooCommerce > Status > Tools > Clear customer sessions also works, but logs out every customer.

fixes.description: Delete 7,000 expired WooCommerce sessions
fixes.sql: DELETE FROM `shop_woocommerce_sessions` WHERE session_expiry < UNIX_TIMESTAMP()

checks.title: Missing indexes and primary keys
recommendations: Missing primary keys or AUTO_INCREMENT usually come from an export/import that dropped table definitions. New posts and options get ID 0 and overwrite each other; fix this before anything else.
Adding an index rewrites the table. On large tables run it in a quiet period, or use an online schema change tool.

fixes.description: shop_posts.ID is not AUTO_INCREMENT; new rows get ID 0. Check the column type before running
fixes.sql: ALTER TABLE `shop_posts` MODIFY `ID` BIGINT(20) UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT

fixes.description: shop_options has no primary key on (option_id). Remove duplicate and zero IDs first, then add it
fixes.sql: ALTER TABLE `shop_options` ADD PRIMARY KEY (`option_id`)

fixes.description: Add index meta_key on shop_postmeta
fixes.sql: ALTER TABLE `shop_postmeta` ADD INDEX `meta_key` (`meta_key`(191))

checks.title: Table engines and collations
recommendations: MyISAM/Aria tables lock the whole table on every write and are not crash safe. InnoDB is the default since MySQL 5.5 and is what WordPress expects.
Tables in utf8 (utf8mb3) or latin1 cannot store emoji and many scripts. WordPress converts core tables to utf8mb4 on upgrade only when the server supports it; plugin tables often stay behind.
Mixed collations cause 'Illegal mix of collations' errors in joins between plugin and core tables.

fixes.description: Convert shop_yoast_indexable from MyISAM to InnoDB (32.0 KB, locks the table while it runs)
fixes.sql: ALTER TABLE `shop_yoast_indexable` ENGINE=InnoDB

fixes.description: Convert shop_yoast_indexable to utf8mb4 / utf8mb4_unicode_520_ci. Converting rewrites every text column; test on a copy first
fixes.sql: ALTER TABLE `shop_yoast_indexable` CONVERT TO CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_520_ci

fixes.description: Convert shop_links to utf8mb4 / utf8mb4_unicode_520_ci. Converting rewrites every text column; test on a copy first
fixes.sql: ALTER TABLE `shop_links` CONVERT TO CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_520_ci

checks.title: Largest tables
recommendations: Large tables: shop_postmeta, shop_actionscheduler_logs. Find out what fills them (logs, sessions, analytics and security plugins are common) before deleting anything.
OPTIMIZE TABLE rebuilds the table to release free space. Run it after the cleanup statements, when traffic is low; it copies the table.
2 tables in this schema do not use the shop_ prefix (another site, an old install or a non-WordPress app).

fixes.description: Rebuild shop_postmeta to reclaim about 120.0 MB
fixes.sql: OPTIMIZE TABLE `shop_postmeta`
